name: SPN AI job scanner
operator: Student Property Network (the vendor, which runs the scanner for its own app)
basis: Student Property Network's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Python scrapers collect roles from UK real estate firms' careers pages into a database; a large language model decides whether each role is accepted onto the list, and accepted roles appear in the app and site.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. The company was interviewed on the record by PrompTugal.news; where an answer rests on the interview page, its note says so. PrompTugal.news belongs to the same operator group as this site, and its page says so; Reach 1 rests on that page alone.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: All three sources fetched on 2026-11-11 (the FAQ page is JS-light plain text; the interview twin and llms.txt are plain text). Each note matches its source. Each span is present verbatim and under fifteen words (I09 span has 14 words, S3 span 14, I20 13). Every URL cited (all five answers) is a key of the scan's captures; not_credited and announced are empty, so no further URL needs checking. Grades documented for statements and observed for the S3 probe are right; mode default is right (the FAQ and llms.txt describe the scanner as it runs for everyone, nothing is opt-in). Indicators fit their text: I08 'executes actions itself' (adds roles to the listings), I09 one domain's data (job postings only), I20 purpose stated, I58 data described, S3 an llms.txt that resolves.

Card computed: A- R1 C- O1. R1 rests on I09 alone (rule: any of I09, I01). O1 rests on I20 with I58 (rule: I20 and any of I56, I22, I58). Autonomy is 0: level 3 needs I08 plus one of I17, I18, I19, and none is credited; level 1 needs I15 (the person operates every action), which the sources do not say. Control is 0: I47 and I38 have no source. The card has level one in two dimensions, so the publication rule (level one or more in at least one dimension) is met.

The only source for R1 is the PrompTugal.news interview page, which reports what the founders said on camera; it is a media page, not the company's own document, and the page itself says the figures are theirs and unchecked. It is also published by a site of the same operator group as this repository, and the page discloses RiskMandate's interest. Grade documented is defensible because the scan's note says the answer rests on the interview, but the reader should know Reach 1 depends on this single source. The interview span is the page's paraphrase, not the founder's words.

I20 and I58 rest on near-identical sentences (the scanner checks UK real estate firms' careers pages), so Openness 1 rests on one fact counted twice. I58 'the data it uses is described' is thin: the sources name where roles come from, not what is stored or how it is used. I20 states purpose (finding roles) but not permitted tasks. Both are within what the rules ask for at level one; the reviewer's call is only that I58 is the weaker credit. Another sentence in the FAQ and llms.txt (members get an alert when a new role matches) adds nothing to either.

I08 is credited but does not lift Autonomy because no I17, I18 or I19 source exists. That is correct: the interview says a language model decides acceptance onto the list and names no step where a person is consulted or approves, but it does not say there is none, so it must not be written as an absence. No answer is missing for I17 to I19 on these three sources.

S1 (in production) is not credited and rightly so: the sources give a count of open roles (175 now) and, on the interview, 27 universities, and the site's own figure of 300+ student members; none is a usage figure for the capability that acts (sessions, tasks, pull requests), and a member or listing count is not one. S4 is not credited and rightly so: llms.txt is a human and agent readable index, not an interface agents call, and no MCP server, agent card or API is described. The scan lists no not_credited entries, although the assessment block records I05 and I57 as lowered by the challenger and the interview names failure modes (accepting bad jobs) that are not published for users, so I22 is also correctly absent. Adding not_credited entries for these, with reasons, would make the card more informative; this is the scan's choice and does not change a level.

S3 is observed by probe and the llms.txt resolves with status 200 on the live fetch. It does not move a level: Openness 3 needs I50 (published evaluations) as well. The captured byte counts differ by a few bytes from the fetched file (llms.txt 8202 vs 8196, FAQ 63105 vs 63099), which is the capture tool counting differently; the hashes were not recomputed and a change of text in the meantime is not seen in the spans.

Round one's note is answered in words (the answer note and the scan note now say the page is the only source for Reach 1 and that PrompTugal.news is of the same operator group), and that is true in the scan. But the disclosure is not the fix: the same card's own FAQ and llms.txt (both captured) already say the scanner reads one kind of page, UK real estate firms' careers pages, and the FAQ says it adds new roles from them. I09 ('works in one domain's data') could be sourced from the company's own FAQ with an exact span, which would remove the dependence on a media page of the operator group and the founder figures the page itself calls unchecked. As it stands the only level one in Reach credits a page from the operator group, and the note's phrase 'the scanner works on job postings only' is the scan's inference: the interview says they collect 'every job they can find' and nowhere says 'only'. Either re-source I09 to the FAQ span, or keep it and word the note as what the page says.

Round-one note kept by the studio ('both meet the rule as written'). Verified: the I20 span (llms.txt) and the I58 span (FAQ) are the same sentence of the same fact in two files: the scanner checks UK real estate firms' careers pages. Rule O1 is I20 plus one of I56, I22, I58, so the whole level rests on one sentence counted twice; remove I58 and Openness is 0, remove I20 and it is 0. I20 is 'purpose and permitted tasks are stated in writing': the cited sentence is under 'How roles are found', it states a method, and no page states permitted tasks. The purpose sentence of llms.txt ('a free app that brings UK real estate careers into one place') describes the app, not the scanner. I58 'the data it uses is described' is met only by naming where roles are read from; nothing describes what is stored, kept or used (members' preferences drive alerts per the FAQ but the data is not described). The credits are defensible only as the minimal reading; the scan should either say in the I58 note that it is the same fact as I20 or accept that Openness 1 is the weakest level on the card. Also not dated by the company: both pages carry no date of their own; the date is the capture.

Round one suggested not_credited entries for I05 and I57; the response says 'Agreed' but the scan still has not_credited [] and announced [] (verified). The assessment block says I05 and I57 were lowered by the challenger and nothing on the card explains why. Not a level change, but a reader of the card cannot see what was considered. Add entries with reasons (I57: the FAQ lists no channel to report a problem with the scanner's output; I05: the interview names the scanner as the founders' own Python scrapers with a model, which suggests in-house but no page says the organisation controls identity, tools and boundaries).

Response 'the few bytes are a page served dynamically; the spans are in both copies' is partly checked. The captured sizes (llms.txt 8202, FAQ 63105) and hashes for those two match my live fetch byte for byte (same sha256), so the earlier byte difference was the capture tool counting. The interview capture hash changed between round one (6d4647...) and now (fe9fc2...), and a live fetch gives yet another hash each time with the same length 4908: only the site version digits in the footer change between deploys (v0.1.1166 in my fetch). So the interview page's hash cannot be reproduced; the spans and the text are stable. Note for the gate and the reader: the hash pins one build of a moving footer, not the statement.

Checked in full: every answer unchanged since round one except the I09 note and the scan note (git diff 4613fe6..HEAD). Spans are present verbatim in the current captured text and under fifteen words (I08 11, I09 13, I20 14, I58 12, S3 14). Every URL in answers, notes, not_credited and announced (compared programmatically against captures keys) is a key of captures: the interview index.md, the FAQ and llms.txt; no other URL in the scan. Grades (documented for statements, observed with method probe for S3) and mode default are right. I08 is correctly credited from the FAQ ('adds new graduate schemes ... as they open'). The response to I08 (the report says no public page states the person's role) is true of data/reports/student-property-network.json.

Arguing against Reach 1: R1 is 'Contained' and the rule is any of I09, I01. I09 is credited from a paraphrase by a media page of the same operator group; the card's standing as the only public level in Reach is therefore the least independent. The interview talks about the founders also using an AI coding agent while building the platform; that is not the scanner's reach and is rightly not credited. If I09 is removed (or re-sourced to the FAQ), R1 survives only on a re-source; without it the card is O1 alone, which still publishes. Does I09 show 'works in one domain's data'? Only by inference from 'every job' and careers pages; no page says the scanner is limited to one domain. Arguing against Openness 1: see the I20,I58 finding: one sentence, method not mandate, credited twice.

Card recomputed with the helper: A- R1 C- O1; used I09 (R), I20 and I58 (O). Publication rule (level one or more in at least one dimension) is met in both Reach and Openness; if either credit fell, the card would still publish on the other, and if both fell it would not (no card below level one in every dimension), so the card depends on the two weakest credits.

New problem, outside the scan file but cited as the card's report: the report fact 'On the day read, the site listed 171 open real estate roles' with span '171 open now' cites llms.txt, but the captured and live llms.txt says '175 open now' for all roles (120 graduate schemes, 5, 19, 30), and the 00:54 and 03:48 captures have the same sha256, so '171 open now' never appears in the captured text. Fix the report (175, read date) or drop the fact. Also the report analysis says 'Disclosed' and 'Contained' carry the card; its 'Contained' sentence says the model decision 'keeps the scanner's work to one domain', which is the studio's reading, not the page's words.

responses.response: Thank you; no change to these answers beyond the I09 note.
Agreed: A- R1 C- O1, and Autonomy is shown as not yet evidenced, never as none.

The note now says the span is the interview page's paraphrase and that it is the only source for Reach 1; the scan's note says PrompTugal.news belongs to the same operator group, as the page itself discloses.
Kept: both meet the level one rule as written. The report says what the scanner reads and does not claim more about storage or use; I58 is the weaker credit, as noted.
Agreed. The report says no public page states the person's role, and does not say there is none.
Agreed; none is credited, and I05 and I57 sit in the challenger's lowered list.
Noted: the few bytes are the capture of a page served dynamically; the spans are in both copies.
